subject.title: # [Bug]: Installer setup wizard has no Back button

question: Should OpenClaw pursue wizard Back navigation through a declarative gateway-provided wizard manifest, a smaller gateway-owned wizard.back/wizard.previous RPC, or keep the current restart/skip recovery model for now?
rationale: Current source proves the Windows client is only a thin renderer for gateway-owned wizard.start/wizard.next frames, so a safe implementation depends on the product/protocol contract maintainers want.

options.title: Declarative manifest with validation
options.body: Have the gateway describe pages, fields, branching, and validation checkpoints up front so Windows owns draft state and normal Back/Forward navigation.

options.title: Gateway-owned Back RPC
options.body: Add wizard.back or wizard.previous semantics to the gateway and have Windows call that for a smaller retrofit with server-owned session state.

options.title: Keep recovery-only model
options.body: Decline per-step Back for now and document restart/skip recovery as the supported behavior until gateway protocol work is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Declarative manifest with validation
recommendation.body: Have the gateway describe pages, fields, branching, and validation checkpoints up front so Windows owns draft state and normal Back/Forward navigation.

likelyOwner.reason: They already gave the most detailed product/protocol direction on this issue and have merged setup engine work in the affected area.
